advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a must-fire eval case to .rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml for a CI-only-trigger plan (recurring/automatic work triggered only by a specific CI system with no operation-linked/in-process fallback), so the new firing behavior has committed regression coverage rather than only rubric-text greps.
evidence: Commit message: 'a plan whose only trigger is a specific CI system is not portable' ... 'the same scratch plan whose only compaction trigger is a GitHub Actions schedule draws zero project.portability findings under the old rubric and one under the new' — verified 'live rather than by wording alone ... Evidence is recorded on the ticket' (i.e. not committed as a test).

tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py:253-258 asserts only that the rubric body CONTAINS the rule text ('### CI is a venue, not a dependency', 'a capability whose only trigger is a specific CI system\nis not portable', 'an operation-linked trigger', 'in-process fallback') — a structural grep, not a firing test.
tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py:110-115 likewise only greps the doc mirror for the rule wording.

.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml:5-6 'four must-fire cases (a reusable-core plan that bakes in an assumption breaking one supported client shape)' — the eval corpus is the committed behavioral harness (line 17-23 deterministic gate: '>=1 finding on a fire case') but is NOT in the changed-files list.

The four must-fire cases PORT-F1..F4 (.rebar/evals/...:27-122) cover a Gerrit refspec, Python-only criteria, a macOS `security` binary, and a cwd-walk; none is a CI-only-trigger scheduled-work plan. PORT-F3 (line 83) references CI only as a venue where the macOS binary is absent — a hardcoded-tool mechanism, not the new no-CI-provider/CI-only-trigger shape.
advisory.finding: The new firing behavior this diff introduces — a plan whose only trigger is a specific CI system (recurring/automatic work with no operation-linked or in-process fallback) must now draw a project.portability finding — has no committed behavioral regression test. The two new tests only grep that the rule's wording is present in the rubric/doc mirror; they never exercise the criterion firing on a CI-only plan, so they would still pass if the criterion silently reverted to drawing zero findings on such a plan. The committed behavioral harness (the balanced eval corpus with four must-fire / four must-not-fire cases) was not extended with a CI-only-trigger must-fire case.
scenarios: A future refactor of the rubric or the criterion routing weakens or reverts the CI-only-trigger rule while leaving the rule's wording text in place — both new tests still pass, and no committed eval case catches the regression.
The criterion stops firing on a CI-only compaction schedule (the exact ce7d-3a15-51e5-4c6a gap) again; only an ad-hoc live run recorded on a ticket would have caught it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fifth must-fire fixture (e.g. PORT-F5) to the eval corpus whose input is a plan scheduling recurring work (e.g. a compaction sweep) triggered solely by a GitHub Actions cron with no stated fallback, expecting a finding whose alternate shape is 'a project with no CI provider'; keep the balanced count consistent (add a matching must-not-fire case such as a schedule that also names an operation-linked/in-process fallback).
